title: Why Onions Make You Cry
description:
Why onions make you cry: cutting an onion breaks open its cells, and a sulphur chemical and an enzyme that were kept apart finally mix. A second enzyme, found by scientists in Japan in 2002, turns the result into a gas that drifts up into your eyes. It sets off the nerves on the surface of the eye, so your tear glands flood it to wash the gas away. The discovery even won an Ig Nobel Prize in 2013. Not medical advice.

Would you eat an onion that can't make you cry?

More true whys: https://www.youtube.com/@truewhys?sub_confirmation=1

Sources: Imai et al., "An onion enzyme that makes the eyes water", Nature 419, 685 (2002); Library of Congress, Everyday Mysteries: "Why does chopping an onion make you cry?"; Ig Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2013 (Improbable Research).
Animation, music and sound: TrueWhys (original). 3D people made with MPFB / MakeHuman (CC0). Fonts: Lilita One (Open Font License).
